The lectures don't help with the homework either.

Dr. Choi's class is definitely a teach yourself class; HOWEVER she is a very nice person and very lenient in her policies. In the class there are quizzes, worksheets, and review problem sets but for the most part everything but the tests are free points. She allows you to work with others on the worksheets in class. The lowest two are dropped! The quizzes and review problem sets are both online and open for some time with multiple attempts. Her tests are really fair, there are a lot of things to go over but she doesn't throw any curveballs on the test, so they are very straightforward. Towards the end of the semester she gave us the option to either drop the lowest exam or get extra credit points. So we could choose whichever one would help our grade more. The final is cumulative but is very fair and as long as you study well you will do good!! I highly recommend her class.

Please dont listen to any dramatized reviews. His exams are straightforward. They are what comes out of his mouth, what is on his slides and most importantly the objectives. The effort you put into the class will determine how you do. He does not curve which no anatomy class has ever been curved which is not a surprise. His exams are not difficult if you put in the work. His jokes can be a little uncomfy during lectures but overall he explains things in a very simple context.

his class was the most boring class i've ever had to take. he would always read straight from the slides in a monotonous tone. that being said, he's accommodating and flexible and his exams are very fair.

First exam was very easy, second two were very hard, last one was very easy. She is very nice and wants you to actually learn the content. I never went to office hours. People were lowk mean to her and I felt bad. The errors on her exams were usually like one word in spanish. Her slides had some spanish but you could understand. Most of her exam questions were fair but some were so weird and actually impossible. She gives practice exams which are just like the regular exams and gives you textbook problems to focus on as well as study guides which are super helpful if you answer all the questions/make flash cards for vocab. Lectures are recorded - would recommend reading textbook chapters and understanding content and watching lectures later or just doing it before class otherwise lectures are very hard to understand.

Dr. Stein is actually a very solid and effective teacher. I had a good time in class and overall learned a lot about microbiology. He uses a lot of interesting examples and the last few lectures on STDs were really awesome. Unfortunately, he is NEVER clear about what he wants as an answer on the exam. I'm not exaggerating - this is ABSOLUTELY TRUE: If your answer to a question is correct but does not appear on the answer key, HE WILL MARK IT WRONG! He says it's so everyone is graded fairly, and if you have any concerns about your right answer (that was marked wrong), you can go to his office hours or submit a regrade. This is terribly disrespectful of our time - we don't have time to go chase points we rightfully deserve. Overall, solid teacher but crappy grader.

very hard, extremely time consuming, nonetheless, I learned a insane amount of useful information regarding cell biology, if ur schedule is already stacked this professor is definitely not ideal but if it's easy you'll be fine just be ready to study a ton and make time to go to his office hours and any exam review sessions he host's outside of class time.

The class was one of the most interesting upper level bio classes I've taken and I enjoyed having Dr. Wu as the professor. It's not an easy class (as one would expect for a 400 level), but she truly wants her students to succeed and offers plenty of chances to boost your grade through clickers, short quizzes, homeworks, extra credit, and even dropping your lowest scores. Dr. Wu is very knowledgeable about the content and super helpful at her office hours, as even a simple 5 minute conversation with her on several instances greatly improved my understanding of the more difficult concepts. Take it from someone who got a better grade in this class than BSCI222 when I say that I honestly think Dr. Wu gives everyone a fair shot to earn an A if you are willing to work for it.

She's amazing. retook gen chem after failing it with dixon and honestly she made it easier and more understandable. dixon made it harder than it needed to be. Take her!!! plus she's so sweet and her study guides for exams are spot on. She understands that the class is challenging and does everything she can to make it understandable. her lecture notes are on point and she's organised. I can promise you that you will not fail if you take her!!! Dixon's gen chem made me feel like i was stupid or something but im not haha.

Jason is easily the best TA for all of CHEM132. I don't know how long he is going to be around because he is probably going to be offered a position as a TA for a more selective class but that just goes to show how good he is. He puts a lot of effort into the class and into the students as well.

If I could rate her less than 1 star, I would. Please, do not take this professor for CHEM135. Every time I show up for a lecture, I feel like my intelligence has dropped substantially, so I stopped altogether. If you have any other choice, please take another professor.

Honestly, such a queen. After Dixon’s Gen Chem, I expected every chem professor to be arrogant and rude, but Koppel was super kind and never passive-aggressive. I actually started in Stocker’s class but switched during the first week once I realized she had no homework — just exams. I wanted some buffer points, and I’m really glad I switched. Koppel gives you 80 points of online homework (easy completion grade — you only need 80%), 40 points of online quizzes (you just keep trying until you get it right), and a few points of extra credit. Definitely helped balance things out. Like most people, I was nervous going into Orgo, but I actually liked it way more than Gen Chem. Koppel gives tons of practice problems, posts old exams (which were super similar to the actual ones), and does late night review sessions. She posts her notes too, but you really need to be in lecture to follow them. Discussion was kind of useless for me. Donnie rushed through like 40 slides and then gave us a bunch of problems we barely had time to get through. It only helped if you already understood the material. GSS was way more helpful (shoutout Jason). I haven’t taken the final yet, but based on the midterms, I think it’ll be fair. She even throws in some extra credit. Overall, I’d definitely recommend taking her.

Even though I came out with a lower grade, i genuinely appreciated having a professor like Davis. His exams reflected the practice exams well enough in order to prepare for exams. Also, he drops one of 4 exams including the final, which was great. The final also was about the same difficulty as the other exams. His TAs were super helpful as well. If you put your time into the course, you’ll come out with a good grade, and should definitely pass considering a 45 is a C- I may not be the best at organic chemistry, but I can appreciate Davis’ drive for us to do well, and the amount of resources and help he provides.

Mignerey is a great teacher who actually teaches us everything we needed to know to do well in her class. Her exams were EXACTLY like the practice exams. She was great at showing us the problems we had to solve and show us how to do it while integrating the concepts.

Genuinely the worst professor in any class I have ever had to take in my entire life. His exams are genuinely impossible, and funny enough, when a student told him this in office hours, he said, "That's good, you'll be ready for the final." So, although half the students in my lecture dropped and most have around a failing grade, at least we are ready for the final. Take this professor if you would like to spend most of your weeks during the semester doing his suggested textbook problems, which, by the way, are very straightforward, such as asking to find a specific vector, set up an integral, etc. However, as soon as you take one of his exams, you are greeted with the most wordy, complicated problems someone could make from the material. For example, on an exam, he asked us to find the total amount of sugar in a gum drop if the amount of sugar at any point in the gum drop is inversely proportional to the distance from the z-axis. Essentially, what I am trying to say is that he provided us with suggested problems often from the textbook which took up hours and hours of our time, only for the suggested problems to be straightforward and the exams to be abstract and complicated and we only had 50 minutes for them. He also references the textbook in class all the time and does problems from it, but for some reason, he does not use the projector in the lecture hall, so if you'd like to fit an entire textbook/laptop on your small lecture desk along with a notebook/tablet just to take notes and be able to follow along, take him. The MATLAB projects we are given provide us with barely any instructions to complete the project, so most students have to use ai to even understand how to complete them. By the way, our first exam average was a 45, and he yelled at us right before fall break started, saying "this is your fault, and you have to bring the average up," which seems normal if you disregard that an entire math lecture scored an average of 45! Our exam averages after that were consistently in the low 60s. I would never recommend this professor to anyone and what really surprises me is that it's not only students from MATH241 posting negative reviews, but also students in his MATH141 and 140 classes.

Professor Conway was great! I barely went to class, but since he uploaded all of the notes and recorded the class it was really easy to keep up with the class. The quizzes every week were really straightforward, and the TA would go over the content right before. The exams were very straight forward as well and the averages were high (in the 80's). The final was co-written by all of the professors in the department, but he went through and made sure that everything was written in a way that was consistent to how he writes his exams. Additionally, he gave out small hints about the final so we wouldn't have to study/memorize unnecessary things. The average on the final, ended up being pretty low but he curved overall grades up one grade boundary. He provided lots of relevant practice problems (exams from past professors and textbook problems). He also was very quick to respond to emails, and very fair with his grading. A couple times I emailed about a regrading request that was denied by a TA, and he took a look himself and gave me back the points and apologized for the TA having been out of line with their response to me. Also, right before the final I saw that something on my first exam had been graded wrong. I emailed him asking if it was too late for a regrade and he made sure the question was looked at and I got my points. My only few criticisms are that sometimes I wished that he would post something written by him so I could see what it would look like before the exam. However, he gave us tests that were written similarly from other professors, so it's not like we were blind sighted walking into the exam. I also feel like because his exams were relatively short, if you didn't know something on one question your grade was pretty heavily impacted.

Dr. Rowland is super friendly and caring. He made an effort to learn every student's name and even studied their ELMs picture to try and remember who people were. I believe over time his organization and content will improve and therefore his overall teaching ability. However, for the time being, those skills were lacking enough that I won't be taking another course taught by him.

He made some errors but not as bad as some other reviewers claim. He's also a very generous grader. I felt like his office hours were much more helpful than going to class, but some of his lectures were quite helpful for the denser material. I would recommend reading the material a day or two in advance that way you know what to expect. Also if you email him ahead of time he with questions he'll give a bit of extra time towards it in class. If not for technical limitations I would take another course taught by professor Fitzpatrick.

Buehrle is very engaging, but at the same time I retained nothing while sitting in his lectures. You could go, but honestly the only classes you need to attend are the review for tests and exam itself. Tests are, as many other reviews have said, much more difficult than the homework on problems done in class, with a lot of problems mixing concepts, but he has used problems from the homework on the tests, so be sure to review the tough homework problems for niche formulas/answers. He gives full credit for correct answer & units, so as long as you have those, you're fine. Textbook is a godsend, reviewing it will be a lot more help, as well as all of the TAs being very helpful.

Makes a simple gen-ed class for mostly non-STEM majors as hard as possible. He curves exams by 5 points, but it is not enough. A LOT of homework, with crazy deadlines (due 2 days after assigning). We had 3-4 homework a week. He also makes you learn a programming language called R, but doesn't let you use R for the exams. He has the curse of knowledge, he lectures like students have the same understanding of statistic as him, a PhD. This class was unnecessarily stressful. He also sends out exam reviews that look nothing like the exams, he loves to throw curveballs. You will have to heavily rely on TAs to understand concepts. He did allow students to do missing assignments on Pearson, so that one nice thing he did.

material is pretty challenging but Jonathan does a really good job explaining it. there's a weekly online quiz that's pretty easy if you just go to class and pay attention, and there are about 8 homeworks the whole semester. the hw's are fairly hard and take a bit of time, but the grading is extremely lenient. exams are also very similar to practice exams that he gives out. hard material but easy to get a good grade if you simply do the work he assigns
Exams and homeworks are needlessly difficult. No flexibility with due dates whatsoever. If you are looking for an easy lab credit, keep searching.

Dr.Choi is very sweet and lenient with her exams. She's not a great lecturer, since she kinda just reads off the slides BUT, as long as you study you should be fine. She lets you either drop your lowest exam or get 15 points of extra credit. There are a lot of free points with the worksheets that you can collaborate on, online quizzes that are pretty easy, and review problem sets, that prepare you for the exams. Her study guides are very detailed, and outline exactly what you need to know/will be tested on. Class averages for the exams are usually 70-80% which is really good. I would definitely suggest taking her class.

Good lecturer? Yes. Looking to slide by without studying every day? Good luck. But honestly, I love the lectures, and he makes them interesting. This class taught me hard work, yet I still had to withdraw... Overall, he's a good option for a professor, but this class will be a wake-up call if you're not used to studying a ton. This class is entirely memorization. He was correct when he said 3 hours a day at minimum for an A.

Dr. Carleton is one of the best teachers I have had. She broke down the content into well-organized lectures. She was very clear with what will be tested and made the memorization-heavy content digestible. She allowed us to make and have a cheat sheet which was a lifesaver. DO THE CONCEPT CHECKS! The concept checks are going to be very helpful. She genuinely is a good teacher and wants you to do well.
Sofia was an incredible TA. She is warm, welcoming, and kind, and she clarified concepts for Dr. Paczolt's genetics class very clearly.

honestly, i didn't learn that much in lecture. found it hard to take notes unless you had a netbook because he teaches off powerpoint slides. all you really have to do to get an A is read the book. the labs were relatively easy and the exams were alright if you keep up with the reading. if you find yourself short a few points of your target grade, dont worry since he'll give out a lot of extra credit towards the end of the course.

Dr Sukharev is a nice guy, can be a bit rude at times, but is nice nonetheless. His lectures were hard to follow at first due to his stuttering, however you get used to it kind of like white noise. Dr Sukharev steadily became a better lecturer throughout the semester, slowly but surely. His exams were not extremely difficult but that averages were always in the 65-70 range. All in all, he’s a nice guy but needs to work on lecturing skills, I must say I did learn a lot from this course by putting in countless hours of study time.

I have taken BSCI410 with her, and I cannot tell how bad it was. She has no idea what she is teaching- slides are not organized and you have to read the textbook in order to understand something in her class. Some materials that we have learned from previous courses, she teaches in a way that you get confused, and in the middle of the lecture, every 5 min she says, I believe, I think, I am not sure.....then why do you teach this course? Homeworks are from articles, and much beyond the materials, you learn. The deadlines are crazy- no fixed deadlines for this class- you need to hire someone just to keep track of the deadlines in this class. The worst class in UMD. My GPA is 3.9 and this class makes no sense to me. Good luck! if you care about your grades or you want to learn something! don't take her.
Literally the worst person ever. Hard to deal with, rude and has an attitude all the time.

You're probably forced to take CHEM132 at some point but if you want to take this class for fun... don't! I was lucky enough to have a great TA but other's are harsh and you literally never even meet the professor... all she did was write the lab manual which has SOOOOOO many typos in it anyway. Even the TA's say that the procedures she writes suck

Alice has a lot of negative reviews on this site, and for good reason. She is terrible with technology, doesn't explain new concepts before jumping right into problems, and can have an attitude when questions are asked. However, the class itself is not that bad. I would say its best to just skip all the lectures and use organic chemistry tutor videos/chatgpt to learn the content, and as long as you grind the practice exam(s) and discussion worksheets the tests aren't that bad, nothing too unexpected. I would recomend taking another professor, but if you have no choice but Alice you can probably manage

Very good professor. No homework so just do well on the exams. She offers so many problem sets and old exams. Discussion was also very helpful. The difficulty of this course is overhyped especially with the amount of practice problems offered. The curve is fine and she will lower it based on how the class does. She does not record lectures and posts her non annotated slides so she doesnt get 4 stars.

Someone also said this, and I agree: I feel slightly misled by past reviews. Coming off of an A in orgo 1 which I did not find difficult, orgo 2 was a whole different experience. I love Dr. Davis, he's such a sweet and good prof, but a lot of the time in lecture, he was kind of all over the place. I also feel like he took too many questions from students and it wasted a lot of time. Otherwise, the way the class is set up is pretty nice, 4 exams total, and your lowest is dropped including the final. The cutoffs are also rly nice, 80 is an A-. There were also 9 bonus points for completion of practice exams, def do them. However the final was incredibly difficult. All in all, be prepared to study a lot for this class. For someone who was taking PHYS161 at the same time, I needed to focus on passing that so I didn't have much time for orgo so just bear in mind that it requires a lot of time and work.

Horrible Horrible teacher. His style of teaching is very confusing and he tends to also skip important stuff. His exams are hard and not in what we learned in class. His class is poorly managed. If you care about your Gpa, don’t take rainbolt

The fact that this professor can teach well is completely negated the exams. They are extremely unfair, and often ask about obscure, convoluted Calc 3 concepts. They are impossible to complete in the time given. Our first midterm average was a 46%, and he would not curve. The exams make up almost our entire grade, so it extremely challenging to do well in this class because of the unfair exams.

I only attended like 6 lectures from the beginning, but from those, he seems to be a great lecturer. He knows what he is talking about, and his accent is a non-issue. He's fairly nice and is very open to answering questions, especially at the end of lecture. Definitely recommend you take him if given the chance.
He is super nice. Just follow his examples and you can do well. We never have any difficult homework/exam for the whole semester. There is no final exam, only a project.

This professor appears to be teaching half the courses/sections at UMD, but then magically disappears and gets replaced by some terrible professor! But on very rare occasion, when the stars align and Testudo rises, the legend Justin will replace Dr.TBA. Overall, any class that Dr.TBA is teaching will be replaced by someone else, so unless you think it'll be Justin, it's probably better to opt to taking a different professor.

Prof. Raj without a doubt made PHYS260 a much easier class than expected. His assignments are super relaxed; ELMS quizzes every week were open note and you had multiple attempts, first two exams were open internet, and he toned down the frequency of the ExpertTA hw assignments two weeks into the course. Teaching-wise, he's pretty good. He emphasizes the concepts before actual computational stuff, so he spends a lot of time deriving the equations we go over in class. Not exactly my favorite style of teaching, but I got used to it eventually. Some of the things he goes over are kinda unclear, so I definitely relied on the textbook during the semester. He has a REALLY soothing voice and dims the lights in the lecture hall, so if you have a late lecture time like I did, or had a long day of class, you might have trouble staying awake during lecture. He also curved like crazy and is super approachable and kind, so I would definitely recommend him.

My goat fr. He IS a little stricter than most professors but I promise its for good reason. SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT and so many resources when it comes to exams. An A is extremely achievable. Only way you can really fail is if you religiously don't show up to class. Feeling extremely confident for the final. My TA and AMPS were helpful throughout the whole semester.

This guy does not deserve his current 3.08 rating. The man does not give any definitions in lecture and just goes over examples without context. His notes on the white board are readable but his handwritten notes are so hard to read. Don't take this man's class if you want to have your sanity by the end of the semester.
RUN WHILE YOU CAN. He does not curve exams (other than the first one), and does not drop any exams. The other professors are so much better for BSCI160

Everyone says his exams are really easy, but I disagree. I follow his review guides and make sure I know all that I need to know, and then I get the exam and still find things I did not study. It's also so stupid that we have 4 midterms and a final, but he does not drop any exams. He also does not curve his exams or his final grades which is super annoying. He talks too much in class which makes it hard to know what will be on the test and what he is just talking about because he likes to talk about biology. His class is not straightforward whatsoever and I wish I had taken someone else.

I really like his teaching style, he likes to draw pictures to help understand the content which is something that works for me. His exams are very fair, if you pay attention and put in the work he is a great teacher. The only negative thing is that he often jumps around the lecture slides and may ramble on specific topics. But overall I would definitely recommend him as a teacher.

Great professor! He really cares about all of his students and listens to any concerns we have about exams, homework, due dates, etc. The class is definitely hard, but the work and exams are fair. you should definitely go to lecture, he posts the slides on canvas, but he talks about them and adds a lot more info that isn’t on the power point. He adds in humor which keeps the class engaging and fun.

I would give 0 stars if I could. She is the worst professor I've ever had in my life. Taking this class with her was so incredibly frustrating because the content within the class is not difficult, what makes it difficult is her slides, exams, and overall organization. Her slides are so disorganized that its extremely difficult/confusing to follow and the little context that is provided within the slides are in Spanish, which I can't understand. She also makes a lot of errors when trying to explain concepts. Her exams are filled with illegible typos and the questions are so wordy and unclear its difficult to understand what is even being asked. This makes providing an answer hard, takes up unnecessary time during the exam, and is even more frustrating when she provides no partial credit or any feedback. Both the 2nd and 3rd exams had failing averages and she responded with telling the class that it was our fault for not asking enough questions or attending office hours. However, when over 100 kids are failing, there must be a fault somewhere else (the teaching). She also did not curve these exams and took 3 weeks to release the grades. Admin was aware and did nothing. This class was so incredibly unfair and didn't even give students the opportunity for success. The reason I have a B is because I taught myself and read the textbook, I give absolutely no credit to Dr. Silva.

Compared to Smith, Stein is a little more difficult. My TA, who took Smith, said the stuff we were learning was harder than what he had learned. That said, Stein really does want his students to learn the material in this course, not just regurgitate the info. He tries to make the information interesting and engages the class through "cool" facts presented at the beginning of each lecture. The book is pretty helpful, so I'd recommend you get it. Also, labs and assignments are actually pretty fun and interesting, but I may be biased because my TA and UTA were awesome. Stein also grades students individually. If he sees you've improved through each exams and do well in labs, he'll definitely bump you up a decent amount.

This class was awful. The exams were super difficult and he was unclear about the content that would be on them. I feel like I worked so hard for nothing because my grade doesn’t reflect the effort I put into this class. His lectures are terrible and difficult to understand. Overall, would not recommend this professor AT all.

Dr. Wu is a very nice, friendly lady and a great professor! The material may seem overwhelming at first but she is very accessible outside the classroom. She also does give open note exams sometimes. Do the homework as this will boost your grade. Participating in class gets you on her good side. Class is difficult just because the material is dense but she does a great job teaching it! would take her again

I took both orgo 1 and gen chem 2 lecture w dr rainbolt. I will say he has a bad reputation because of his mean outwards demeanor, strict policies, and hard class. However, ultimately hes very helpful and explains well in his office hours. His content prepares u extremely well for the mcat. he has everything organised into a singular packet for the entire class. His classes were also the best to take if you dont come to class because his recordings and packet covered everything. He also has a strong curve. Orgo was brutal, but sad to see him leave tbh.

never met her, so can't say anything about her personality but lab manuals have extreme typos, post lab questions make no sense, mid term and final are very hard as well. if you have to take her for lab just make sure you go to office hours for the post lab otherwise the questions can be interpreted 10 different ways.

Alice began with a confident tone, Then left our brains to suffer alone. Each lecture teased, then quickly stalled, Sixteen weeks, academically blue-balled. Her grading’s chaos, her slides a mess, My GPA’s now crying in distress. She spoke in riddles, slow and tall, Queen of confusion, long may she stall.

haha... yea all the past reviews? they stay in the past. Easy exams? easy A? BS. Ever since she got confronted by the chem department she has been making her exams at least 20x harder than last semester. She gives you no practice exams (only the final) and the practice work (pp sets) she gives us are way easier than her actual exams. so you basically get barely any preparation for her midterms especially in the concept of an actual exam. For example when you are doing the practice sets shes giving for each chapter you are only studying for one chapter at a time, you really dont get to sit and have an exam like practice session (bc none are provided). She explains things well i say, but again not enough to prepare you for an exam. you get 8 tries on all the hw so its actually impossible to not get 100% on them....but they really dont weigh much on your grade either. Praha (her TA) made no sense to me. he talks sooooo quietly so if u want to go to discussion go early and sit in the front. and all the practice wok in discussion were also too easy compared to the final. Also the cutoffs are INSANE. u basically dont know ur grade until the end of the semester but even with that the cuttoffs are brutal. 57% for a C- while in other classes a 58% is a B.

Live love davis. Coolest professor known to man. Would love to sit down get a beer and do endless mechanisms with him. Hard class, lectures are a bit disorganized, but reorganizing the content helps you study and actually figure out the material (which is hard in itself).
I love prof.Mignerey! She taught us everything that we needed to know for our exams. Exams were very fair and her office hours were really helpful. Overall 10/10 and would take her again.
Really good at lecturing, but the exams are EXTREMELY difficult and have no curves. Unless you want to sink all of your time preparing for his exams, I recommend taking ANYONE else.

Super cool professor, and I'm ngl he has a ton of aura with how he looks so casual when teaching the class in just sweats and jeans, with a slightly disheveled look like you know this guy is smart af. But moving onto the class, he actually did a great job of teaching this class and the class is super fair and there are not any tricks. I've had other professors for math where they are reading basically verbatim from the textbook and just throw a bunch of information onto you, and you get super stressed out because you have no idea what's important and not. For this class, Prof. Mellet had a pretty streamlined version of the course which was great. The notes that this course are based on are from another professor called levermore, who has an insane complex set of notes for diff eq. Ngl that guy's a genius but no normal student can even understand wtf 70% of his notes even mean. Mellet did a great job of providing just the important stuff that you need to know. Yeah, sometimes he'd go into some wild proofs, but that was just to show how you get to that, and he even says u don't need to memorize it. I will say in the last 3rd of the class on systems, lowkey pay attention to everything because I did not and I got my ass kicked on the 3rd midterm. His grading is also very fair. He always provides practice midterm/final questions that have appeared on his past exams to use as study material, and the actual exam very closely mirrors those topics. But if you manage to mess up an exam like me, he makes Ur worst exam only 10% of your grade, so it actually does not hinder your performance by much, so shout out to him. Ngl the final was hard ash as well that was the first math exam I've had where I did not finish it entirely. But I think he curved the class a bit due to that. Overall definitely take him he's a great professor

Really nice guy who takes the time to answer questions and make sure you understand. Teaching style is like Justin's where he will present you a topic, give you examples and then expects you to be able to replicate it. He makes exams weighted less than most math classes, so if you are a bad exam taker you will love Lutian. He also responds to emails instantly.

I highly recommend taking a course with Gulick if you can. He's a super nice professor and loves to teach his class, and as others have said he has a very quirky personality, which I think is a huge benefit to keeping the class interesting. Additionally, I've always had no problem reaching out to him for help as he's quite welcoming and never once was condescending towards any questions I had, regardless of how silly they may have been (something that unfortunately can't be said about many of my previous math profs). I agree that the way he runs through proofs in class can be a bit too fast sometimes, but going to office hours has helped with that along with going through the textbook while doing HW. While the homework definitely becomes a pain in the a** as the semester goes on its definitely a helpful way to keep you on track and in my opinion is better than having a few major assignments as it gives you a little bit more leeway in the event you forget to do an assignment or submit it late.

He's a very sweet guy and tries to be very accommodating of his students but my god was his class awful. He's a bad lecturer (pauses for 5 seconds every 3 words, does not make it clear what he is telling us/the greater significance of what he is telling us, making it difficult to take notes) so you have to learn everything from the textbook. He doesn't model his teaching off of what's on the homework or what he puts on tests. If you take this class with him, you will need to self-teach

Let me start this by saying Prof. Fernandes is a great guy, super chill, mildly funny, and jerky like most math professors can come off as. With that being said... based off his teaching style and behavior during content dissemination, it became clear to me that he has never taught a 100 level course before, which makes sense as most of his previous reviews were of his STAT400 level courses. STAT400 and STAT100 are not the same thing, one is a early intro class and another has students that know what their doing, because he has only ever taught in that environment he reflects that in his teaching of STAT100. He's not bad but you'll definitely have to take advantage of your resources.

I truly do not know why Dr. Preston has a decent rating. Nice person, but should NOT be teaching any remotely difficult math courses. Starts writing on the board while rambling without any real explanation, leaving students in the dark during lectures. The only piece of advice I have for someone taking his classes are to stop showing up to lecture and read the textbook instead. It will be a much better use of your time. In addition, the homework problems were unnecessarily difficult and often used tricks not at all taught in class.

I am not one who enjoys evolution or ecology but Dr. Shapiro was a really great professor. Even if it is not something you are interested in, he is super passionate about what he does and posts all his lecture slides which is helpful. His tests are extremely fair and my best tip to doing well in his class is go through all the powerpoint slides, take notes and know the definitions of the bolded words, then go to office hours for any questions. If you are able to spit back out the concepts from the powerpoints, then you will do well on his exams. Plus he lets you bring a notecard to each exam and drop one test. Also the review sessions in office hours are recorded and it helps so much! I would take this class again.
Honestly, not a bad teacher, I would recommend her. Tests are easy, she's very lenient in my opinion.

Inaccurately preps students for exams, makes multiple choice questions confusing purposefully. Anatomy is a pretty straightforward subject but the way he teaches and his lecture exams make it pretty difficult. Would recommend taking someone else if you can!!

I loved Dr. Karen. She is the sweetest professor I've had so far and she clearly cares about what she's teaching. The only reason I took off a star is because classes are boring and she kinda just reads from the slide. I also had a hard time telling what to study or telling how specific the exams would get about the content. But other than that it was chill. There are concept checks that are ungraded practice DO THEM literally like 30% of the first exam multiple choice I already knew because I did the checks. Could have gotten an A if I studied more and went to class :/

Literally wish I could give this 0 stars. WORST professor I've ever had. Like I can't even explain with words how horrific. Class averages on tests are like 50% and somehow she thinks that's normal? Clearly she has some serious self reflection to do. I don't know how she's even still hired. Also can we talk about how half her lecture power points are literally in Spanish...do I look like I speak Spanish? Do yourself a favor and SPRINT in the opposite direction because this teacher will have you contemplating your life. If you think she's good, stop lying to yourself.

Dr. Stein really wanted us to "understand" a lot of things. His lectures slides were very engaging. I do have to say that his course is a lot of work. He is somewhat approachable, yet I feel that his test seemed unfair at times. He even claimed that "I feel that this was a bad test, since majority of the class got x amount of things wrong." But, if you are up to date with everything, and work hard, hopefully, you will be able to do well in this course. Overall, I thought it was okay, the Module 3 about HIV, and immunology was great :]

I will start by saying he is a very nice person, however nice doesn't exactly equal good. For his first time teaching in undergrad, I feel as this class had been nothing but a social experiment. His study guides for each exam before the final did not prep anyone for the exam, whatsoever. He literally released them 1-2 days before the final, and sometimes he forgets to add tings, so when we think we have it all, there is still more, and it made it worse when the extras he added did not show up in the exam. His quizzes that are also supposed to help us with exam prep were released the day before the exam as well, so no help there. I say that they were useless homework materials that were not graded. He literally said in class, "Don't worry guys, next semester I will get it right." So I wasted a good chunk of time and money trying to do well in a class, he's teaching for the first time, and said he would put in effort next semester. The biology department has been no help either, even after a class full of emails, I was the only one to get a reply and they said they were looking into this. Nothing changed. We are supposed to receive extra credit, yet someone in the class group chat announced, he will only get extra credit if he feels like we earned it. While we were promised for Exam 2, all that showed up would receive extra credit. There was also an extra credit assignment, that when we asked for help because it is a program he uses, he told us to call the IT department over Thanksgiving break. Only a few students got it to work, and when they did, most didn't know how to use the program to find the answers. This course had been a displeasure to take and I wish I dropped in when I had the chance to.

Dr. Wu is definitely my favorite professor so far- she goes out of her way to make herself super accessible for office hours (which were moved to Zoom) because she really cares about her students. The information is definitely not easy but she doesn't expect you to memorize facts- as long as you get general mechanisms/concepts down you should be good. Her exams are really similar to her homeworks which makes studying a little easier. But there is a good amount of work in this class (clickers (basically participation), mini short answer questions, quizzes, homeworks, and exams) so definitely NOT an easy A. But if you're willing to put in the effort and watch the lectures and go to office hours, you're in good shape to do well.

She's a sweet teacher and cares about her students, which you won't find everywhere. She answered numerous questions in class and during her office hours and provided us with practice problems. Her tests were fair, and honestly, not hard if you studied the material she provided. She also gives a lot of partial credit on exams, which is nice. I only got one B on an exam in the class because of this. On average, her students got better grades than the other 131 classes because she didn't include incredibly challenging problems in her tests. I recommend reading the textbook if you don't understand some information, and for extra practice problems, which she lists in her slides. The homework did act as a good cushion and wasn't that challenging. CHEM131 is a weed-out course for STEM students, so it's unrealistic to expect the class to be easy. But if you need CHEM131, take it with Ms. Stump.

Please for the love of god do NOT take this “professor”(the reason I put it in quotes is because she isn’t a true professor, just someone who knows about Chem). If you do you’re asking to fail the class. She is well known around the campus as one of the worst “professors”. How she still has a job I have no clue. The only way I ever understood any of the material was from my friend who got a 5 on AP Chem in high school and from the TA in discussion. By the way that TA, Matthew Wrotny, was the best dude ever. Always had a good sense of humor and made class fun. Back to Alice… she never explains HOW she does the problems. She might be 90 years old but she goes so fast in lecture to the point where she is practically done the problem when you finish writing it down. So you can’t fully understand the problem because you look up and she’s almost done with it. So in summary, going to the lectures is basically pointless because you never retain any information from her not even explaining what she’s doing. It’s like she expects that we already know all of the material and this is just review. For example, anytime someone asks a question, she speaks to you in a tone like you’re stupid and should keep your mouth shut. And by the way she is the absolute WORST with technology! The first lecture, it took her half the class to get her slides pulled up on her iPad. Then the next day she tells us that she bought a whole new iPad just for class and has been practicing with it every night. But it doesn’t seem like it though because she’ll try to go back 1 slide but in reality skip 5 slides forward. It’s a totally pointless lecture and you have to be able teach yourself or go to a lot of tutoring if you have her. But I STRONGLY recommend you to find any other professor that is not named Alice Mignerey because you will be in for real treat if you have her.

She was alright. I did enjoy the way she explained things and I felt like the lectures didn't cram too much in, until the last exam. However, the whole class consists of only 4 things in the gradebook, 3 midterms and 1 final. She gives you homework to work on your own but it doesnt get put into the gradebook. Another thing is that she doesnt curve as much as I'd hoped. I scored around an 80 on both the first exams (way above the average) and still was fighting for a B towards the end. If you can take another professor I would, but she's not the worst professor for Orgo.

Be prepared to teach yourself the content. He has clicker questions which quiz you on the content that he just went over, so if you cannot learn on the spot, you are screwed. About half of the questions on exams come from previous/old midterms he has posted and the textbook additional problems. For some mechanisms he says not to refer to the textbook and his method, making it confusing to understand what he is looking for. His grading is nice where he guarantees an 80 is an A at the beginning of the semester, however, I took this when Davis was teaching and had a nice curve, dropped exams, did not give clicker questions, and gave extra credit which was infuriating knowing we had to work 10x harder with harder material. To succeed, I recommend Professor Dave explains or jOE Chem on Youtube for concepts you do not understand.
Horrible teacher, has a terrible attitude. Exams are not fair at all and he expects us to know things he didn’t teach. Just don’t take him if you value your gpa and mental health.

Dr. Williams makes math241 as hard as it can possibly be. Do yourself a favor and take anyone except him if you do not want this class to consume your life in an effort to get even just a B. As of writing this review, 2/3 of the exams we have taken have had an average grade of failing and he is giving us an exam the wednesday before our final which is the following monday. It's almost like he takes pride in writing the hardest exams he could possibly come up with. If he would just curve the class so there would be a slightly reasonable grade distribution, then I would have far fewer problems with Dr. Williams, but it seems like his ego doesn't allow him to consider this. I would highly recommend not taking Dr. Williams.

Dr. Conway replied to most of my emails in minutes! Seriously, he is so awesome. Dr. Conway taught so well. Every lecture was recorded and each topic consisted of a good balance between theory and examples/applications. The quizzes were easy. The 3 Matlabs took an hour or so and were not difficult (example code were given, and only minor tweaks were necessary). The midterms did not contain anything unexpected - you will score high on the exams if you do and understand the suggested exercises for each section. The final was somewhat difficult, but this was not Conway's fault because Mellet was the person who wrote it. Conway was very nice and told us what was for sure to not show up on the final. It seemed like Conway wanted to tell us more about what to expect but was unable to because the course chair did not let him :(. All three of Conway's midterms had a good grade distribution, but the final was somewhat skewed. Again, it was not Conway's fault, and to compensate for this, there was a generous curve. Roughly 90 ended up being an A, and 86 an A-. Grading: - 10 quizzes (worth 17%, lowest 2 dropped) - 3 Matlabs (worth 6% each, total 18%) - 3 exams (lowest worth 8%, other two worth 0.17%) - final exam (worth 23%) Just take it with him. Trust.

Class follows a predictable format: a few lectures, groupwork in class, then homework due, and then the cycle repeats. 12 topics and 4 exams that aren't cumulative. so each exam touches on roughly 3 topics. My one gripe is that sometimes the homework problems he writes himself can be a bit nasty to do. Usually they don't take too long, but you have to sit and think about them for a bit. I have learned a lot though!!!

Above average. Besides reading from the book, he only gives slightly different proofs. He gives a lot of homework. His exams are difficult, especially the midterms, because of a shortage of time. The final is easier, with double time and 1.5 times as many questions as midterms. A difficult question in midterm 1 is similar to a homework problem. Another difficult question in midterm 2 is related to the Darboux theorem (which is not included in the textbook).

Great professor! Super sweet and accommodating, very passionate about the subject. This course is absolutely awful but he makes it more bearable, which I really appreciated. Our first two exams were open notes/internet and he's very available over email! Overall a great physics professor, if he's available for 260 definitely take him.

Professor Griffin was by far the best professor I had this year. Despite this class having over 250+ students he tries his best to get to know all of his students, especially during office hours. Math is my worst subject BY FAR, but he made this class very easy and provided many resources for students to succeed in this class. He has many extra credit opportunities and provides identical study guides when it comes to the 3 exams we have in this course. Also, the AMPs are very helpful, and they are a huge reason why I am ending this semester with an A. Finally, it can get annoying when Prof repeats the same message regarding mandatory attendance, headphones off, problem sets, etc... but he genuinely cares about the success of his students.

He is a nice guy, but his lectures were very hard to follow and were often very unorganized. He never went over definitions, and just did random examples without specifying what he was covering. Homework assignments were long and typically about material not covered in class at all, so it was necessary to self teach from the textbook which lacks examples as is. Lastly, sometimes he was condescending when people asked questions.

His class can definitely be boring at times but overall it's really easy to follow! His lecture slides are really basic and most of the important information actually comes from his talking so I think going to lecture is worth it in order to take notes that aren't just on the slides (which are always posted). He's really nice and passionate about the topic which is refreshing and cracks random jokes which are pretty funny. He also allows an index card for each midterm and the lowest midterm grade get's dropped which I think is super helpful. Overall his exams align greatly with the notes and examples he gives in class, even if they're extremely niche, which is why I'd say it's important to pay even a little bit of attention to what he says. I think if you just pay attention to what he says and put in a little effort to understand the concepts, with the notecard too the exams should be fairly simple and his class should be easy to pass!
he is fine i dont feel like he is a good professor though I have had to heavily rely on other classes and videos and readings to get me through this class

I love Dr. Bennett's teaching style. He doesn't go slide by slide but bounces around to set up foundational knowledge that is super helpful for understanding concepts in the long run. Anatomy is definitely a difficult class but he gives you realistic expectations and an objectives list that is super useful for studying. Exams are long and specific but mostly fair. He makes a lot of innuendo-laced jokes that can be hit or miss, but definitely are memorable (which he says is his goal, so students remember content). My only complaint is that he doesn't record lectures or have a zoom option. I would definitely take him again.

Fletcher is the nicest guy you'll ever meet; he makes the class environment super welcoming towards new students and won't hesitate to help you. However, I found his exams kinda difficult; they are very detail-oriented, and while it holds true that everything comes off of his slideshows, his slideshows are each about 75 slides long, and there's around 10 slideshows per unit. It's a lot of content to cover. If I could retake the course, I'd start reviewing information earlier before exams because a lot of it is memory based. I also think his lectures are more on the ramble-y side, but he records them, so you don't have to attend if you don't want to. Overall, great and approachable guy!

Not sure why someone gave her 5 stars.... I would recommend any other professor. Her schedule is partially in Spanish as well as the occasional slide which she doesn't even address or translate. There have been multiple times in lecture where she will misspeak and move on without correction. She is extremely difficult to communicate with and she does not respond well to feedback despite this being her first semester teaching. The first exam average was high but this was likely because it was a lot of 170 content. Her following two exams had much lower averages. The workload is unnecessary and poorly paced through the semester. She frequently will move due dates without announcing it. Overall, I do not recommend this professor and my TA has echoed the same statement.

This class was very easy. Although his lectures are boring and he tends to try very hard to make lectures exciting, they don't really make students want to stay in class. You must go to lecture 20 times at least to get the clicker points. Overall, Stewart is a very good teacher if you listen to what he says. He wants his students to pass so utilize his weekly study questions. If you answer these you will be prepared for the tests. Another great thing Stewart does is posts the final question to each test and a sample test for every test. With these and Koofers tests (which were exactly the same tests we were given this year) it is impossible to not get an A. Good luck in Micro!

-The course consist of material that are not prerequisite to this class. For example, genetics (from BSCI222) and biochemistry (from BCHEM461/462). -Rarely record any of his lectures. (only recorded about 20% for this semester) -Always show up 10 minutes late. (No, I am not joking. Lectures do not start after 10 minutes into the class EVERYDAY). -Lecture slides: 80% consists of diagrams that you have memorize and know how to DRAW them. Very brief explanation on each topic. -Lab is the only thing that is keeping up your grades and it is with another instructor/TA. Easy lab grade as long as you complete your assignment. -Quizzes: Literally posts them the night before the midterm and it won't be open until late afternoon. -Midterms: No multiple choice. All short answers and some of them you have to memorize and draw the diagrams. You have to label them as well. Early this semester, on the day of midterm, he allowed students who arrived early to get a head start of the exam (about 15 minutes head start). Which is very unfair to the people who have classes before this one. -Extra credit assignment: Little to no instructions. People complained about technical difficulties with the app that we were suppose to run. When we emailed him about the issue, he would asks you to refer to an IT. -Midterm study guide: (sigh) Not very helpful...only about 10% of the stuff will be on the midterm. On the third midterm, he even send out annoucements about the things that we were suppose to remember yet none of the related question showed up. -Final exam study guide: For this semester...two parts. About ten pages combined. After completing the questions you will get about 41 pages of information. (Not joking)

Dr. Wu is a phenomenal lecturer but most importantly a kind person. This course can definitely be a challenge, as it was for me, but Dr. Wu made sure I stuck with it and did my very best. She even requested a 1-on-1 with me when I failed the first exam to better help me. There were three exams, lowest score was dropped, and the final was optional!

(Fall 2024) To Friedman, With Honesty I can't speak it plainly, So let this be verse— A truth wrapped in rhythm, A blessing, a curse. This class isn’t easy, No gentle A's here, I faltered through hardship, With doubt and with fear. Your lectures, they wandered— More name than idea, Theory, not practice, The concepts unclear. Clickers required, Attendance a must, But learning felt distant, In whom could we trust? My TA was harsh, His words raced like rain, No kindness to anchor, Just silence and strain. I earned but a C Still, I’m not alone. Even my friend with an A Let the same truth be known. No chem before this, No prep in my pack, Yet hope found me later— In Orgo, I came back. So if you fall short, Know you’re not through. There’s still light ahead, And it will carry you.

terrible terrible terrible. Curves the class mainly based off of if u did the homework. IF you get 96% on hw then you should be able to pass. You won't learn anything but you have a chance to pass even if ur exam grades are trash. I can't emphasize how bad it was. good luck

Let me start this review by saying she is no means a bad person. She seems very friendly, has a good sense of humor, and tries to adapt the lecture to suit multiple teaching styles (learning with Pokémon was my favorite). Ever since she was investigated, her class has become SO MUCH HARDER, even compared to other orgo 1 classes. While she is good at lecturing and provides notes guides (which I found really helpful while studying), she has not been able to provide us with the necessary resources to pass the class at a harder level than she used to teach it at. We were told to look at notes and complete problem sets to help with studying. NOT ENOUGH. The exam content was always so much harder and a lot more niche. Basically, memorize all her notes AND THEN SOME. She also rarely records classes which doesn't help... Also, the lack of information rlly made the whole experience stressful. We weren't told about any of the grade cutoffs, just a "best guess." After discussing the grade cutoffs with people in other classes, I was shocked at the difference (Our C- is 57% and my friend's B cuttoff is 58%... actual insanity). HWK is 8 attempts and the one with the highest score is kept, so I had no issues there. Discussion is a waste of time. Praha seems like he is very knowledgeable but he moves very quickly. More than once I've seen people raise their hand, not get called on for a couple minutes, and give up asking a question. He also doesn't post the answer keys to the worksheets, which is of no help when you're trying to review on your own time. GSS was a godsend though, definitely attend those if you can. All in all, I chose her class because I'm someone who inherently struggles to grasp chem concepts. Don't be fooled by past reviews </3

Such a nice guy!! Definitely try to take him if you can. Lectures are engaging, clear and very productive. Dr. Davis's exams did get progressively harder, but they were generally very fair. Make sure to study a lot as exams are the only grades in this class.

Great professor, knows what she is talking about. The classes she teaches are difficult classes so this is why she tends to get bad reviews. Her test are fair and just like any other teacher teaching the course.

Had him for Calc 3 after withdrawing from the same class the previous semester bc of a terrible lecturer. Gave up going to his lectures like two weeks in and self-studied; all he does in his lectures is copy his exact notes that he posts online onto the board with almost no clear explanation or organization and even less attention to whether or not students are actually comprehending what he's writing. I actually left classes more confused about the concepts than I did going in with my previous Calc 3 knowledge. He grades the entire class based off two exams, 3 MATLAB assignments (which literally said at the top that they were Justin's and edited for fall 2024 despite me taking this class in fall 2025). Take 241 with someone else. The one benefit of his class is that there was not a wide range of topics on the exams. Study exactly what's on his review sheets and the exams are fine, although very high stress as there's only 4-5 problems per midterm (which means your entire grade hinges on like maybe 20 problems total including the final). There was also quite a generous curve, with B- being a 70. However, that doesn't really make up for the fact that pretty much the entire class hinges on your ability to self-teach and get lucky with getting everything absolutely correct on exams since there's so few opportunities to earn points.

He is literally the goat. He is super nice, he responds to emails very fast, and very accommodating. The class is a very easy A if you put in the effort to go to his class and do the review problems he says to do. - Records all his lectures + posts his notes online - Weekly Discussion Quizzes (2 lowest dropped and your TA reviews content before the quiz) - 3 Free Matlabs - 3 Midterms (all very fair) - Final was a little difficult but curves the class to account for this

The worst professor I've ever had at UMD. You will be undergoing an entirely self-taught class if Jakobson is your professor. I will say that he is polite and always willing to answer questions, but that is if you can even tell what is going on in the class to formulate a question to begin with. He began the class writing on the chalkboard, albeit never turning around to actually talk to the class - just talking at the board about seemingly random topics. As of the second week of class he just shows us grainy pictures of notes (not even a PDF scan!!) on the projector and reads over it. It's seriously hard to learn anything from this prof, as half of the time I'm not even sure what the current topic is (his handwriting is not the best).

Professor Du is a great professor. She comes to class with very organized and structured notes, which she then posts after each class so if you miss a day you won't be behind. However attending class is still beneficial because she doesn't just mindlessly write the notes on the board, she explains them as well, especially the more complicated proofs. Her lecture is very structured as well. She presents a definition, then a theorem, and then a proof, in that order. So if you like an organized prof you'll like her. The homework is hard but prepares you for the final and you have one homework a week (but it takes about 2-4 hours generally so it's best to not do it last minute). I got a 100% on the first midterm and a 66% on the final, so it's definitely a tough final (average on it was 55%) but she curves the class accordingly (86% for the class got me an A). Math 410 is a very hard class and likely the first tough proof based math class you'll take at UMD. And I think taking professor Du is very beneficial if you plan to take more rigorous proof classes. Also she has a very easy to understand accent so don't worry about that either.

Love Raj, terrible at physics, for some reason they decided to have the final cowrote by him and Buehrle, as expected, the average was a 39% Not his fault. Still way better than any physics professor at this school.

Take STAT 100 with any other professor!!! Griffin records attendance at lecture and discussions, which are not necessary at all. To miss ONE CLASS you need a University Level excuse like a doctors note literally saying you're incapable of getting out of bed. He's not empathetic at all and pretends like his class is the most life changing and important class in the world. He spends at LEAST 25 minutes of lecture (the whole class is 50 mins long) complaining about people not showing up or not doing work or not paying attention to him. He yells at us basically everyday like a high school teacher begging students to put in effort. STAT 100 is super easy and all the requirements for his class are completely unnecessary. Highly DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I had Fernandes this past summer for STAT410 and it was his first time teaching the course. Usually students take STAT400 first before STAT410 but this was not the case for me. Fernandes did an amazing job explaining the course material I would say he's just as good as Justin when it comes to teaching. Also if you ever had questions about the homework, course material, or R projects you could do to office hours and he would walk you through it. He turned STAT410 from a difficult to easy course and was extremely approachable definitely easy to get at least a B and with a little bit of extra studying you can get an A.

I would recommend taking Dr. Ngeve for BSCI 160. She's engaging, nice, and explains the content well. There aren't many homework worksheets, but some of the ones you will do are a bit lengthy, but not difficult. There are also discussion boards each week, which are easy and are a grade booster. Dr. Ngeve gives PLENTY of extra credit opportunities, so do it because they're saving my grade right now. The exams (consists of content from the lecture slides and content in the textbook that isn't really touched in class) are pretty lengthy and are a bit difficult, but it's not too bad if you study outside of class (notes, lecture slides, review questions, kahoots, etc.) and she lets you have a small note card during exams. Also, your lowest exam score gets dropped, so that's nice!

This class is very much teach yourself, but it is very manageable. All her test questions are about the slides from class, and they are all very straight forward. I never payed attention in class, but spent the week before the exam studying, and got A's on everything. If you are good at memorizing take her, because questions are word for word the slides. She also lets you either drop the lowest test grade, or get 15 points of extra credit at the end of the year. And the final exam is 50% new lecture topics from after exam 3, and 50% everything else, but it is all from previous test questions. If you don't mind taking time to go over your notes to make sure you understand it, take her. I thought it was a really easy and straightforward class. Lectures are just a little boring

I like the way he teaches. He explains things very well but he does go off on tangents sometimes. He tells you everything you need to know in lecture but does not record his lectures, so if you don't go to lecture you're kinda screwed. He makes funny jokes to keep the class entertained and awake. He also connects the information to things in the world.

Like everyone says, she’s a kind and sincere professor. I just feel the lectures are her reading off the 50 or so slides where we don’t even have time to write much of anything down. Each lecture is pretty loosely related to each other so it doesn’t really matter too much if you skip one because you can watch the recording. I felt she was an alright prof and attribute most of my success to the cheat sheet for exams and just reviewing lecture recordings because I skipped a decent amount of lectures.
Rude and condescending during office hours. I got the impression that she didn't want to teach. Tests have trivial questions that can be difficult to study for. Should be a curve, but there isn't.

Dr. Smith was a good teacher. Sometimes it can be a little frustrating b/c her slides don't seem to have a lot of substance to them, but by the end of the course, you will learn a lot! I recommend doing the study questions and going to review sessions to ask about any questions you might not be able to answer. I also recommend looking over the PAKs before the exams. BSCI223 overall is easier than most bio classes but there are a lot of small, kind of busywork assignments. I really liked the lab because you learn a lot of techniques and you are not penalized for mistakes during procedures, so you aren't afraid to try new things.

If you get to know Sukharev, you'll find that he's pretty decent and nice with a bit of humor. He does, however, seem to carry around a condescending & lackadaisical attitude. But, he is NOT a good professor. He is terrible at explaining concepts, and he teaches new material by using even more convoluted and complex terms & principles. He almost expects us to already have a background in cell biology, biochemistry & mammalian physiology, even though these courses are not prerequisites for the class. There is also some math & physics that you'll have to know. Expect to learn a lot of material on your own or through the textbook. His study guides are always loaded and are either a hit or miss. There are 4 exams (3 during the semester & one cumulative final), and what was on the test is COMPLETELY different than what he puts on the study guide. He even admits that his study guide was too loaded at one point, and then for the next exam, he proceeds to double the information. In addition, there are no practice exams, he doesn't release an answer key, and doesn't go over the correct answers. He also spends a day reviewing for an exam and specifically tells us to memorize certain topics, then proceeds to not even put them on the exam. Also, the exam is ALL free-response. No multiple choice, true/false, etc. The course is loaded with insane amounts of material & detail (just under 40 lectures with each lecture being at least 30+ slides - also I forgot to mention 95% of slides are diagrams & pictures with barely any words, so you'll have to record on your own because he'll only record maybe every other few lectures for whatever reason), and oftentimes, he doesn't even finish the lecture. Transitions between slides are nonexistent, and it feels like you're jumping every all at once. You're also better off betting the over on class time as he starts class late and ends the class late because spends the last few minutes + more quickly going over 10 slides that he didn't get to. I hope you find a way to stray far far away from him. Sukharev is a good person, but he is an awful instructor and is extremely disorganized, unprepared, and seems to not give an F about his students. He claims to give out an extra credit assignment that he calls easy, and then we find out that it's a whole coding program that researchers & graduates use in which we have to learn by ourselves to create molecules and answer difficult questions on it (the program is called VMD). His stutter and accent don't help the situation any better. He promises he'll go easy on the exam, and it turns out to be twice as hard as the previous. There are no TAs for the class, no discussion, no guidance, no nothing. I had a very difficult time getting used to his lecture style. Dr. Wu is a good professor and actually wants her students to succeed and understand the material. After failing general chemistry my first semester of freshman year, taking Ms. Stump my second semester was life changing! She explains things so well and is super helpful. She is very personable and friendly. Her homeworks are like the exams and the exams were never extremely hard. I studied A LOT so I had always felt prepared fro the exams. Her lectures can be kind of dry sometimes but not always! I seriously reccomend her for gen chem

She is goes on irrelevant tangents and loses the plot often making lectures useless. Goes through the chapters quickly and sometim3s pulls concepts and numbers out of thin air without ever teaching them. I hope you like solely relying on the textbook and youtube!

Orgo is a hard class, and it'll be a hard class but Dixon definitely made an attempt to make it a forgiving class. the tests are very forgiving since she has buffer points and extra credit. HOWEVER the extra credit is very hard and you need to work on it with other people. make a study group asap since it'll help with her HWs which are again extremely hard. use GSS, office hours, discussion, etc to get the most out of this class or else you'll be behind. she goes through lectures quickly which is a bummer but she teaches everything that you need for orgo 2. overall a good prof but asks for a lot of time. many people hate her but me personally, i think she's a good prof, and I would rather take her class again than be the first one in the 100 men vs. 1 gorilla.

Dr. Davis was sociable, receptive to questions, and seemed passionate about chemistry. He explained things fairly well and connected them to real-life concepts (like common medicines, animals, etc.) His practice exams and wealth of past exams, as well as all the lecture notes being posted on Canvas, were extremely helpful. Davis also offered extra credit points before each exam and dropped our lowest exam grade. That being said, it’s hard for me to understand why people love Davis as much as they do. His lectures felt pretty disorganized (especially compared to Hirschauer's orgo 1) and his test difficulty jumped by magnitudes after the first exam. Test questions were sometimes weirdly misleading or unrelated to lecture material. The class was entirely exam points — no homeworks or quizzes to buffer your grade. Davis also made his final cumulative for the first time this year, which seemed unnecessary. I was lucky to have some incredible TAs (shoutout to Nick and Edward) who made this otherwise okay class into a great one.

Unfortunately, the first time I took CHEM271 I barely passed. This time around I had Dr. Schech, and it didn't take long for me to realize that she is absolutely the best chemistry lecturer I've ever had. Her lectures are incredibly organized and she records them so you can watch them over or catch up if you miss class. She is super thorough in her explanations and often engages with the students so it's hard to doze off. Honestly, I often get bored in chem lectures but the way she presented the information was genuinely interesting at every moment. On top of the discussion worksheets and homework, she also posts recordings of her going over extra practice problems that are incredibly helpful. The exams were fair so as long as you do the practice problems/homework and understand the nuances of the concepts (which are explained in lecture) you should do well. She also responds to emails quickly!

Professor Zhao is a great teacher in my opinion. He's clearly very passionate about math which makes his lectures engaging, and his course is designed in a pretty fair way (40% final, 50% over 2 midterms, 10% discussion quizzes). My grade is so low because I completely flopped on the first midterm- it really wasn't that bad but I didn't prepare at all. Locked in for the second one and did much, much better. He does a pretty good job explaining the concepts, but he emphasizes derivations and concepts over examples. I personally love the theory, but for a class designed for engineers, I can see why people have some issues with his teaching style. He also goes pretty fast, and his handwriting isn't the cleanest I've ever seen, so the blackboard can get a little messy at times. He answers questions pretty well during lectures. There was no homework in this class, so you have to practice on your own time. He does post example problems from the textbook to work on though. There were also no matlab assignments. Sometimes the course can get a little disorganized; It took a very long time to post the second exam on elms, and the elms page isn't the most organized. Overall, Professor Zhao is great. He's very reasonable, a good lecturer, and a fair grader. Strongly recommend him
Great professor. Balances conceptual and practical, relates concepts across different sections of the class and real-world topics, friendly, helpful, accommodating.

Dr. Rowland is one of the nicest professors I have had; he prioritizes you learning the content and the class emphasizes consistent, project-based work. I felt like whenever I went to class, I went to learn about real-life applications of linear algebra instead of trying to pass a class for credits. With that being said, the only thing keeping him from 5 stars is that he can be disorganized or do incorrect arithmetic at times and that makes some concepts difficult to understand at first.
She is the most prepared lecturer I've ever had in a math class. Super smart and can always answer questions in office hours. totally fair grader.

BE WARY! Although his first two exams were open book and open internet, the final plunged us all into the deep end with a class average of a 41%. He teaches very theoretically and spends tons of time deriving equations instead of giving examples. I found that it was more valuable to read the textbook on my own rather than attend lecture.

I got 98% on the first exam and 101% on the midterm. Do all the homework, go to every lecture, and take every extra credit opportunity you can and you will no question end up with an A. Yes, he's a little strict but it's worth the A. Lots of study sessions led my amps and amazingly organized lecture slides. TAKE GRIFFIN FOR A IN STAT100

I felt like Preston was an awesome teacher. He clearly cared a lot about teaching students as best he could, and provided a lot of resources to help us do so. Classes were flipped, so the normal lecture time was office hours for those with questions, which was helpful when I had them. The tests and homeworks were fair, albeit a little challenging, but grading was always quick, fair, and transparent. Your worst of the three exams counted for less than the other two and you could drop a homework, which was appreciated, and cutoffs have a 91 count as an A and not an A-, which is helpful too.

While I love this professors personality and teaching style it’s simply too much content which makes studying harder. Exam content is too extensive. Water break questions, kahoots, book, PowerPoints, and online lectures still aren’t enough to ensure a decent grade.

There is a lot of material in this class and going through 70-80 slides per lecture is a lot to digest. While her exams were fairly easier compared to other professors, it took a lot to study for them. Everything on the slides are fair game. I personally did not end up using the textbook as I found the wording to make me even more confused. You have to really teach yourself for this class. All of this being said, Dr. Choi is very sweet and will explain anything to you with patience.

Bro... one of the worst professors I've had. Dr. Fletcher is a great professor! He records all his lectures, drops the lowest grade in each category, and has very fair exams. However, I feel like the fact that he records lectures compensate for this since you can always catch up on information you missed later. Overall, nice guy and I would for sure recommend him for 207.

She is the worst professor I've ever had. This class has stressed me so so much! after the 3rd exam the class average is 72% and there is no curve. Dr. Stein is a really good professor. He tries very hard to make this subject fun, by giving assignments that are actually real fun. Overall it is easy to get a B in this class (because the lab grade will boost your grade a LOT!), but getting an A requires a lot of effort. Even then I would still take Dr. Stein because he is a great teacher, he explains things well, he hold review sessions every week, and his assignments are really fun (content-wise).
